summary: State 122f40f8cef6d0a7 is 1.560x over the baseline at 240 pairs (CI 1.557 to 1.563; 1.566x at 60 pairs), battery 98/98; the previous recipe 5553e312 was 1.49x. It is built on a new source state 92815d94 (the baseline source with HB=4 heads per workgroup and NCG=2 column groups, grid [cdiv(H,4), B, 2], still 256 workgroups), whose amdclang build is a loss on its own (0.863x), so the gain over my own source state is about 1.81x (ratio of two timings against the baseline, not a direct compare). The machine-level work: (1) key loop with 16 global_load_dwordx4 per iteration (256 B = two full cache lines per lane) and the 4 query rows read as wave-uniform scalars (s_load_dwordx16 in two phases per 64 B chunk, 128 scalar-operand v_fmac per chunk) instead of amdclang's 16 per-lane query loads per 4 key loads; (2) value loop with 16 row loads issued up front from a running pointer, accumulators as (x,y)/(z,w) pairs with p selected by op_sel, LDS p reads pipelined. Case: not at the memory floor in the headroom sense (headroom 6.9) because the KV cache is re-read by every workgroup; the lever that paid was fewer re-read bytes per workgroup (each workgroup reads all keys but only half of the value columns). Probes put the key phase at about 62 % of the remaining 170 us.

friction: 456f50a21daa83a5 passes static_check and fails the battery deterministically although liveness(5553e312, .LBB0_7) reports every register it adds as dead across the block. The only structural difference from the verified parent is 24 outstanding vector loads with s_waitcnt vmcnt(20) and vmcnt(16). I did not run the discriminating test (same code with vmcnt(0)); if waits above vmcnt(15) or more than 16 outstanding loads are a real limit, the s_waitcnt checker should say so.

static_check reports 8 to 16 undefined_read warnings on amdclang's own phi copies (.LBB0_40 / .LBB0_38, v_mov_b64 of registers written only on some paths, harmless under EXEC). They are identical before and after an edit, so a real undefined read introduced by an edit in the same registers would be hidden among them; a diff of warnings against the parent would help.

liveness: the conservative live_in/live_out lists all 128 VGPRs for every block of this kernel and is two pages of output; only the classical section and dead_across_block are usable. Registers that a block itself uses as temporaries (written before read) are not listed as free, so I derived them by reading the block.

state(id, full=True) of a 1271-instruction kernel exceeds the tool result limit and is diverted to a file; the edit action text of the parent (hundreds of lines) is echoed in full at the top of every state() call, which is most of that size.

%rep cannot index a list (register bases 22,26,...,50 then 62,...), so non-contiguous register sets need one %rep per contiguous run; a list form such as `%for D in 22 26 30 62` would have cut the value-loop edit by half.
No tool shows which SGPRs/VGPRs hold constants that are only used by code I have replaced; freeing SGPRs for a second scalar-load set needed manual searching (it turned out not to matter).

Could not go to HB=8/NCG=4 in the budget: amdclang's value loop for 4 heads already spills 15 VGPRs and needed a full hand rewrite; a transform that rewrites a 'loads + pk_fma into accumulators' loop into the all-loads-up-front form would make each new source variant cheap to try.
source(like=baseline, defines=...) cannot change HB/NCG because the baseline text uses plain #define rather than #ifndef; the whole text had to be resent.
lessons: mla_decode: the time per workgroup follows the bytes one workgroup (one CU, 16 waves) reads, not the total traffic. HB=4 with 128 workgroups read half the total bytes and was no faster than HB=2 with 256 workgroups (1.36x vs 1.49x). Keeping 256 workgroups and cutting bytes per workgroup paid: HB=4 with NCG=2 (all keys, half of the value columns per workgroup; 6.8 MB instead of 8.9 MB) went from 1.358x to 1.522x with the same key loop, and 1.56x with the value loop rewritten.

Loads in flight is the wrong description of what paid in the key loop. A rolling window that keeps 12 to 16 global_load_dwordx4 in flight but issues each lane's 64 B chunks one step apart measured 1.288x, the same as 4 loads per iteration, against 1.49x for 16 loads issued back to back (256 B = two whole 128 B cache lines per lane). My reading, not measured directly: with 16 waves per CU and a 32 KB L1, a line touched in two separate steps is fetched twice; issue all loads of a cache line back to back.

Serial scalar loads for a wave-uniform query row are free here: removing 7 of 8 s_load_dwordx16 pairs with their lgkmcnt(0) waits per iteration changed nothing (177 us vs 170 us, probe). Two phases of 32 SGPRs per 64 B chunk are enough for 4 heads; do not spend effort on a second SGPR set.

Value loop rewrite (all 16 row loads up front, pair accumulators with op_sel instead of v_mov shuffles, pipelined LDS reads) is worth about 3 % on this kernel (1.522x to 1.566x at HB=4; 4 % at HB=2 in the earlier session).

Split on the best state (170 us): key phase about 106 us (62 %), everything else including launch about 64 us. In the key phase the fmac work is roughly 20 % by instruction count (512 v_fmac per wave per iteration, 16 waves on 4 SIMDs); the rest is waiting for key rows at about 43 GB/s per CU.
A source variant that is a loss as an amdclang build (0.863x: per-lane query loads, scratch spills) can still be the best base for machine-level work: 1.81x came from two loop rewrites on it.

amdclang's phi copies after masked loops read registers that are only defined on some paths; when replacing a loop, check which registers the blocks after it read (mirror copies such as v45/v43/v49/v47 here) and which it expects zeroed on entry, since the even halves of pair accumulators were not initialized by the original preheader.

session.final:
The session ends with a verified state at **1.560x** over the baseline (240 pairs, CI 1.557–1.563; battery 98/98), up from the earlier recipe's 1.49x. The state to ship is `122f40f8cef6d0a7`, and the report is filed.

## What the winning state does

- **New source base (`92815d944a9a3d93`)**: the baseline source with 4 heads per workgroup and the value columns split over 2 workgroups (grid `[cdiv(H,4), B, 2]`, still 256 workgroups). Each workgroup reads all keys but only half the value columns. As an amdclang build it is a loss (0.863x), so it does not become a new baseline.
- **Key loop rewrite (`fc098aafd201c604`, 1.522x)**: 16 key loads per iteration, i.e. 256 B or two whole cache lines per lane. The 4 query rows are read as scalars in two phases per 64 B chunk.
- **Value loop rewrite (`122f40f8cef6d0a7`, 1.566x at 60 pairs)**: 16 row loads issued up front, pair accumulators selected by `op_sel`, and pipelined LDS reads of p.

Relative to my own source state the gain is about 1.81x; that is a ratio of two timings against the baseline, not a direct compare.

## What did not work

- **Rolling window of loads** (`53cc2c03c942a68d`): keeping 12–16 loads in flight but issuing each lane's 64 B chunks one step apart measured 1.288x, worse than its parent's 1.49x. My reading, not measured directly, is that a cache line touched in two separate steps is fetched twice.
- **24 loads in flight** (`456f50a21daa83a5`): still fails the battery, deterministically. It is not a clobbered register: every register it adds is dead across the key loop. The only structural difference is 24 outstanding loads with `vmcnt(20)`/`vmcnt(16)`; I did not run the test that would confirm this.
- **Pipelining the scalar query loads**: a probe that removed 7 of the 8 serial load pairs per iteration showed no gain (177 us against 170 us), so I did not build it.
